invariant_argument: IncidenceStructure owns private counts and normalized BTreeSets. Constructor success proves counts match storage, every line has at least two distinct points, and all points are in 0..num_points. No mutator exposes the representation. Duplicate lines are intentionally retained and the pair predicates count indexed lines, so duplicate-line evidence cannot pass a partial-linear check when it shares a pair.

TooSmall precedes resource admission. Checked num_points squared and that product times lines.len() are each at most 16777216; the latter bounds all distinct-point-pair line membership checks conservatively. Raw lengths sum to at most 1048576 before any BTreeSet construction. These are scalar/work envelopes, not byte-precise allocator guarantees. Old arbitrarily large requests may now refuse intentionally.

For each 0<=p1<p2<n, both predicates count exactly the indexed sets containing both. The nested ranges enumerate every unordered distinct pair once, with p1+1<=n. Comparing the count to one gives exactly partial/linear incidence. Shared borrowed views cannot invalidate the constructor invariants.

For affine p in {2,3,5,7,11,13}, trial division rejects precisely the remaining composites in 2..=13. Point encoding x*p+y bijects the bounded coordinate square to 0..p*p. Every vertical line has x=c and every other line has y=m*x+c in F_p. Distinct x admit a unique slope/intercept by the field theorems; equal x and distinct y force the unique vertical line and exclude slope lines. Small modular representatives compute the field operations exactly, with intermediates <=168 and no division in Rust. Every admitted prime and line equation is independently checked, and the concrete Fano table has a kernel-checked unique-line theorem.

Ray admission checks n*n<=1048576 before matrix allocation, so n<=1024; n*(n-1)<=1047552 fits 32/64-bit usize. It scans the first unequal width before any pair computation; then checked n*width bounds all borrowed input cells and checked pairs*width bounds dot terms by 16777216. n=0 uses zero width/pairs; n=1 still admits its input width even though it has no dot calls. Width zero and zero vectors are intentional non-physical cases, giving all off-diagonal pairs orthogonal.

With equal widths, zip visits every coordinate. Starting at exact zero, checked_mul and checked_add either return the corresponding integer product/prefix in i64 or return a typed error before corruption. Induction on the coordinates proves exact successful dots. This is a deliberately narrower checked-prefix domain than all integer dots with in-range final sum. Both multiplication overflow and cancellation-after-prefix-overflow have independent witnesses.

The initially false square matrix is written for each i<j exactly when the successful dot equals zero. Symmetric writes make adj[i][j]=adj[j][i]; diagonal cells remain false. Dot symmetry is proved for integer lists. All public inputs are immutable borrows or consumed owned values, no partial matrix escapes an error, and defensive private partial writes are not a public transaction guarantee.

All 22 production bodies meet CCN<=10, cognitive<=14 and control nesting<=3. Incidence creation scans raw entries and builds bounded ordered sets; predicates cost O(n*n*L*log(1+S)), where S is maximum line size, under the product envelope. Ray output uses n*n bool cells plus n Vec headers; dot work is O(n*(n-1)*width). Shape preflight scans at most 1024 row lengths and owned intermediate output is dropped on every error. Standard Vec/BTreeSet allocation, compiler, thiserror and Rust runtime remain trusted; no OS out-of-memory recovery or constant-time property is asserted.
